gaps.lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

gaps.lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.

gaps.answer: sure how I would have reacted
gaps.lead: It's difficult to know what my reaction would have been in that situation.
gaps.hint: difficult to know = not sure how
gaps.explanation: 'I'm not sure how I would have reacted' — a hypothetical past.

gaps.lead: Darius soon recovered after the operation on his knee and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.sentence: After the operation on his knee, Darius ___ and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.explanation: 'Recovered soon' is expressed with the noun: 'made a quick/fast/rapid recovery'.

gaps.lead: Given that he has no experience, will Glyn be able to do this job?
gaps.sentence: Will Glyn's ___ his ability to do this job?
gaps.hint: no experience = lack of experience (noun subject)
gaps.explanation: The noun subject 'lack of experience' takes the verb 'affect'.

gaps.lead: You must complete the form in ink.
gaps.explanation: must complete → must be completed (modal + be + participle).
